title: Autoscaler suppression during regional surge causing reserved capacity shortfall
creator: Ethan Clarke
description:
Summary: During a coordinated customer load spike in eu-west, the dedicated autoscaler failed to scale reserved GPU capacity in time, leading to sustained headroom shortfalls and elevated tail latency for several enterprise tenants. Customers reported 429s and sudden throughput degradation despite available cloud quotas. This ticket tracks investigation, mitigation, and follow-ups for a permanent fix.

Evidence observed: 
- Autoscaler decision logs show a continuous suppression flag set for the region between 2026-03-09T22:10Z and 2026-03-09T23:25Z.
- Metrics indicate request queue growth and steady increase in pending allocation time (p95 from 120ms to 2.1s).
- Burst credits were consumed faster than predicted for multi-tenant pools; however, headroom telemetry reported non-decreasing free slots (false-positive).
- Correlation with control-plane GC cycle: a leader promotion coincided with a transient sensor lag.

Repro steps (sandbox): 
1) Spin up a reserved pool in eu-west with small-tenant weight skew and burst enabled.
2) Replay customer production traffic trace (s3://redwood-prod-traces/eu-west/2026-03-09) with 3x multiplier over 10 minutes.
3) Observe autoscaler logs and headroom telemetry; verify suppression flag behavior when sensor heartbeat misses.

Initial root-cause hypothesis: 
- Race between autoscaler horizon projection and the reserved-pool sensor refresh where a stale headroom reading led to a suppression heuristic flipping on.
- Suppression logic treats too-short horizon projections as safety and inhibits scale-ups; combined with burst-accounting underestimation, this prevented timely allocation.

Immediate mitigation performed: 
- Rolled back a safety change in autoscaler suppression heuristics (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/6243) to remove overly-aggressive circuit-breaker for single-sensor misses.
- Applied a hotfix to bypass suppression if pending-allocation-time exceeds 3000ms (deployed 2026-03-10T04:14Z).
- Communicated mitigation and ETA to affected customers via incident comms doc (https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/dedicated-eu-west-2026-03-09).

Validation: 
- Post-fix canary in eu-west showed allocation latency back to baseline within 6 minutes and no 429 spikes for the replayed trace.
- Telemetry dashboards updated: reserved_pool/headroom_raw and autoscaler/suppress_count now have finer-grained tagging for sensor origin.

Open action items (next steps): 
- 1) Add verifier that cross-checks headroom telemetry against allocator state before setting suppression (owner: Priya).
- 2) Improve burst-credit model to account for multi-tenant skew and transient surges; add simulation harness tests (owner: Backend-Sim).
- 3) Harden leader transition path to avoid stale-sensor windows (owner: Control-Plane).
- 4) Run a region-wide chaos test that injects sensor heartbeat delays during Canary (owner: SRE).

Acceptance criteria: 
- Autoscaler does not suppress scale-ups for sensor-lag windows under realistic load patterns.
- Regression tests added to CI that replay the 2026-03-09 production trace and assert no sustained headroom shortfall.

Artifacts & links: 
- Incident timeline and postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incident/dedicated-eu-west-2026-03-09/postmortem
- Hotfix PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/autoscaler/pull/6243
- Canary deployment dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/allocated/canary-eu-west-2026-03-10

Notes: This ticket focuses on the autoscaler suppression path; related allocation accounting bugs are tracked separately. Coordinate with PM to ensure customer-facing RCA is aligned with postmortem wording.
